A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SLA research. The text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.3 are readable and support comparison; the additional page in v2 reflects reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation comparisons, ablations, and timing measurements in Section 6, plus image-generation experiments in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3 and the kernel-speed and generation-latency comparisons in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The attention-mask prediction, sparse and linear components, learned projection, forward/backward algorithms, and Appendix A.3 optimizations are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same private collection of 20,000 five-second 480p videos and ImageNet at 512 × 512. Video- and image-generation task coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Full Attention, Sparge-F/T, VSA, VMoBa, and the same component ablations; Figure 6 retains FlashAttention2 and the same sparse comparators. The changed SageAttention citation does not change an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Figure 6(a) changes the reported kernel-speed annotation from FLOPS to 1/t. This is a limited metric-reporting revision: Section 6.1 still defines FLOPS as full-attention operations divided by latency, and no recalculation or experimental rerun is documented. Training budgets, model configurations, and other evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same sparse/linear fusion, activation-function, and top-k ablations. The attention-weight analyses and qualitative examples, including Appendix A.1, are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain single-value reporting without adding repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, Figure 6's plotted numbers, and the qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, SLA retains 2.74T FLOPs in Table 1 and FID 31.49 in Table 3. The speed-label revision introduces no changed numerical values, rankings, or reported findings.

T1.justification: The attention decomposition, equations, gradient derivations, Algorithms 1–2, and Appendix A.3 complexity reasoning are unchanged. Figure 6's relabeling adds no mathematical derivation or formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same hybrid-attention contribution and claims of 95% computation reduction, 13.7× kernel speedup, and 2.2× end-to-end speedup without degraded video quality.

C2.justification: The sparse/low-rank explanation, interpretation of linear attention as learnable compensation, and ablation interpretations are unchanged. Section 6.3 retains the qualification that the higher-sparsity baseline timing comparisons are not quality-matched.

D1.justification: The disclosed training steps, batch sizes, block sizes, hardware, baseline implementation details, and appendix optimizations are unchanged. Both abstracts retain the same promise of future code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhang et al.'s survey of efficient attention in Sections 1 and 7 and replaces the SageAttention3 reference with SageAttention2++. The broader positioning among sparse, linear, and hardware-efficient attention methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited terminology, spelling, citation, and version-header edits, including changing kernel 'FLOPS' to 'Speed' and correcting 'Origianl' to 'Original' in Figure 6. The prose and section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figure 6(a) receives revised titles and speed-axis labels, and Figure 6(b) receives a spelling correction. The conclusion and references reflow, leaving one reference on a nearly empty page before the appendix. Other figures, tables, and appendix displays are unchanged apart from pagination.

improvement.justification: v2 retains the same scientific content, empirical support, and reproducibility information. The citation updates and typo correction provide limited polish, while Figure 6's new 1/t label remains unreconciled with Section 6.1's FLOPS definition. These localized edits leave overall paper quality materially unchanged.
